item.title: Assistant Sports Minister raises concerns over Garvey Park conditions
item.description: Concerns were raised earlier today on the conditions of Garvey Park in Tavua after students were digging out stones from the ground. Assistant Minister for Sports, Aliki Bia had raised the alarm saying this is not good and it does not portray a good image for the development of our rugby.
item.content:encoded:
Concerns were raised earlier today on the conditions of Garvey Park in Tavua after students were digging out stones from the ground.

Assistant Minister for Sports, Aliki Bia had raised the alarm saying this is not good and it does not portray a good image for the development of our rugby.

Bia says the welfare of students and players is paramount.

This is also because it is the first time that Garvey Park is hosting the Vodafone Super Deans National Quarterfinals as well as the Weetbix Raluve Quarterfinals.

Concerns have also been raised on how hard, and dusty the ground is with two players already being taken off the field in ambulances.

The U18 quarterfinals are currently underway at Garvey Park between Ra High School and Ratu Kadavulevu School, which will be followed by Cuvu College vs Nasinu Secondary School at 3.05pm.

At the HFC Bank Stadium, Lelean will play Rati Navula at 4.30pm, followed by Grammar and Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute at 5.55pm.

item.title: Live Updates: Fijiana 12-27 Springboks
item.description: The Springboks have scored first in their historic Test match against the Vodafone Fijiana XV in Fiji to lead 5-0. 12" Adi Vani Buleki burning up the sideline before the ball gets turned over by the Springboks.
item.content:encoded:
The Springboks have scored first in their historic Test match against the Vodafone Fijiana XV in Fiji to lead 5-0.

12" Adi Vani Buleki burning up the sideline before the ball gets turned over by the Springboks.

14" Buleki looking dangerous with ball in hand breaking through and clearing 30 metres but no support was on hand.

16" Beautiful break up the sideline by the Springboks No. 8, they are camping just outside the Fijiana's 5 metre. Pick and drive and try to the tighthead prop. RSA 10-0 FIJ

23" TRY!! The Springboks hooker gets her name on the score card and now the whole front row has scored a try each. RSA 15-0 FIJ.

26" TRY!! Varanisese Qoro with a beautiful individual try and some amazing footwork. Converted by Litiana Vueti. FIJ 7-15 RSA.

29" TRY!! Springbok women strike back. RSA 22-7 FIJ.

item.title: Taveuni residents still waiting for water as shortage worsens
item.description: Residents in parts of Taveuni say the ongoing water shortage is becoming increasingly desperate, with some families still waiting for water despite reaching out to the Water Authority of Fiji for assistance. A resident from Naselesele told fijivillage News that after contacting WAF to arrange a water cart to fill his household tanks, he was asked to provide his details and was told someone would c
item.content:encoded:
Residents in parts of Taveuni say the ongoing water shortage is becoming increasingly desperate, with some families still waiting for water despite reaching out to the Water Authority of Fiji for assistance.

A resident from Naselesele told fijivillage News that after contacting WAF to arrange a water cart to fill his household tanks, he was asked to provide his details and was told someone would call him back with a quotation.

However, he says several days have passed and he has not received a phone call or an email.

The resident says the situation has become critical as families continue to struggle without a reliable water supply while the dry spell persists.

Last week, WAF told fijivillage News that prolonged dry weather had significantly reduced water levels at the Mua raw water source, affecting water production and supply to several communities across Taveuni.

The Authority says it was carrying out water rationing and valve operations to manage the limited supply, adding that normal water supply would only be restored once there is sustained rainfall and the island's raw water sources recover.

Questions sent by fijivillage News to the Ministry of Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Management last week on what assistance is being provided to affected communities remain unanswered.

We have also sent further questions to the Water Authority of Fiji regarding the concerns raised by residents, including the reported delays in arranging water deliveries, and are awaiting a response.

item.title: GCC wants Constitution changed to ensure more women enter Parliament
item.description: The Great Council of Chiefs wants Fiji's next Constitution to guarantee more women a place in Parliament, saying it is time to move beyond promises and take action. In a statement, GCC Chairman Ratu Viliame Seruvakula says the Council is proposing a legislated quota requiring between 30 and 40 percent of Members of Parliament to be women.
item.content:encoded:
The Great Council of Chiefs wants Fiji's next Constitution to guarantee more women a place in Parliament, saying it is time to move beyond promises and take action.

In a statement, GCC Chairman Ratu Viliame Seruvakula says the Council is proposing a legislated quota requiring between 30 and 40 percent of Members of Parliament to be women.

He says any government elected after the 2027 General Election should no longer leave it to political parties to decide how many women they will field as candidates, with measures to improve women's representation instead written into the new Constitution.

Ratu Viliame says Fiji's current constitutional and electoral system has failed to create equal opportunities for women to participate in national and local governance, despite many capable and experienced women being ready to serve.

He says local government elections should also be used to develop future women leaders before they progress to national politics.

The GCC Chairman says many women want an electoral system that allows them to build direct relationships with their communities, be accountable to voters and earn election on their own merit.

He also says women have always played an important leadership role within the vanua , contributing to community development, preserving culture and supporting traditional obligations.

Ratu Viliame is urging the Prime Minister and the Government to support the Council's proposal, saying Fiji deserves a Constitution that gives all citizens an equal opportunity to serve their country.

item.title: Seaqaqa cane farmer to receive land lease next week after delay - TLTB
item.description: The iTaukei Land Trust Board says a Seaqaqa cane farmer who raised concerns about delays in receiving her land lease will receive the document next week. This follows concerns raised by cane farmer Sheila Wati during the Special Committee on the Sugar Industry's public consultation, where she said she had already paid the lease premium but was unable to start planting cane because she had not rece
item.content:encoded:
The iTaukei Land Trust Board says a Seaqaqa cane farmer who raised concerns about delays in receiving her land lease will receive the document next week.

This follows concerns raised by cane farmer Sheila Wati during the Special Committee on the Sugar Industry's public consultation, where she said she had already paid the lease premium but was unable to start planting cane because she had not received the lease.

Responding to questions by fijivillage News, TLTB Chief Executive Officer Solomone Nata says the lease has now been stamped by the Registrar of Titles in Suva and is being dispatched to Labasa today.

Nata says Wati is expected to receive the lease document next week.

He also apologised to the tenant for the delay.

When asked about the reason for the delay, Nata says the lease was lodged with the Registrar of Titles in May and has just been processed and returned.

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka, who chairs the Special Committee on the Sugar Industry, had earlier requested Fiji Sugar Corporation Chief Executive Officer Bhan Singh to take Wati's details so that a response could be provided.
